title: Understanding the Scaled Inverse Tangent Function
text: The scaled inverse tangent function is defined as $$f(x)=\frac{1}{\pi} \arctan\left(x\right)+\frac{1}{2}$$. This function is similar to the logistic function in that it maps any real number to a value between $$0$$ and $$1$$. Can you think about why this property is important for classification?

title: Comparing Tail-End Behavior
text: Both the logistic function and the scaled inverse tangent function approach $$0$$ as $$x$$ approaches negative infinity and approach $$1$$ as $$x$$ approaches positive $$\infty$$. Why might this similarity be useful when constructing an ROC curve?

title: Evaluating the Function's Range
text: What is the range of the function $$f(x)=\frac{1}{\pi} \arctan\left(x\right)+\frac{1}{2}$$?

hintAnswer: The function outputs probabilities between $$0$$ and $$1$$.
title: ROC Curve and AUC
text: Why is it possible to construct an ROC curve using the scaled inverse tangent function?
choices: The function outputs probabilities between $$0$$ and $$1$$.
